expectations.text: Says what counsel must confirm: at minimum whether closing floats with the extended diligence period (also acceptable: day-count convention, the 5:00 pm cutoff, weekend or holiday handling)

The float question is treated as answered and the seller's contrary reading is dismissed as 'a weak argument'; the check items are addressed to the user, not counsel.

expectations.text: Compares the lender's August 18 funding to both closing dates (three days after August 15; ahead of September 4) and says title's August 15 calendar needs reconciling
expectations.evidence: 'funding on August 18 is 17 days ahead of the contractual closing date'; against August 15: 'a buyer who is not funded until August 18 looks late'; 'Title company: August 15 is the old date and needs to be corrected'. 3-day figure not stated.
No invented term relied on; counting rule disclosed ('I counted June 2 as day 1'). 'Treat 5:00 pm on August 5 as the deadline' is a conservative working rule.
Takes the lender's date at face value but does not call it a commitment or verified; asks to confirm commitment and rate lock run to September 4.
No call script or spoken opening anywhere in the response.

Unqualified headline and rights conclusion: 'Closing is September 4, not August 15.'; 'funding on August 18 is 17 days ahead of the contractual closing date. There is no default problem.'; 'a buyer who is not funded until August 18 looks late when it is not'. The sole next step acts on it: 'Send the title company the Second Amendment today and ask them to move closing to September 4.' The only counsel reference is a trailing line ('have counsel confirm against the full PSA and both amendments') that conditions nothing.

'Next step: Send the title company the Second Amendment today and ask them to move closing to September 4.' Single action; owner is the reader by imperative, not named. Borderline pass.
No work record; ends with a counsel disclaimer.

notes: Math correct, but the most assertive response: unhedged headline, 'no default problem', and a next step that has title move to September 4 before any confirmation.
